title: Olivia Rodrigo's Dream Festival: All Girls, All Day, All for a Good Cause!
summary: What if a music festival was just for girls—and every ticket helped make the world better for women? That's exactly what Olivia Rodrigo is doing! The "Vampire" singer just announced her very first festival, Daisy Chain Fields, happening August 29 in Irvine, California. And the lineup? It's a who's-who of girl power: Chappell Roan, KATSEYE, Doechii, and even rock legend Stevie Nicks will perform. Olivia herself will hit the stage too, along with bands like Bikini Kill and Garbage. She posted on Instagram that she's "never felt more excited" to share the news. "I've had a dream of doing this festival for years," she wrote. Here's the coolest part: every single penny of profit goes to charities that support women and girls. That means groups like Planned Parenthood and Baby2Baby will get a big boost. Olivia has been on a roll helping others. Last year, her Guts World Tour raised over $2 million for her Fund 4 Good, which fights for reproductive rights and against domestic violence. She even won an award from Planned Parenthood! Daisy Chain Fields is inspired by Lilith Fair, a famous all-women festival from the 1990s started by Sarah McLachlan—who is also a special guest at Olivia's event. So grab your flower crowns and get ready to rock out for a reason. As Olivia says, "Joy, community, and music can be the drivers of meaningful change." Sounds like the best kind of party!
why_it_matters: This festival shows that music can be more than entertainment—it can raise money and attention for problems that affect women and girls, reminding you that even fun events can help make the world fairer.

background_read: Olivia Rodrigo is a Grammy-winning singer-songwriter who became famous for songs like “Vampire” and has used her voice to support women's rights.
Lilith Fair, the festival that inspired Daisy Chain Fields, was created in 1997 by Sarah McLachlan (a Canadian musician) and toured North America, raising millions of dollars for women’s charities.
Irvine, California, is a city known for its large outdoor concert venue, the FivePoint Amphitheatre, which often hosts major music events.
Article_Structure: WHO: Olivia Rodrigo and a lineup of female artists including Chappell Roan, KATSEYE, Doechii, Stevie Nicks, Bikini Kill, and Garbage
WHAT: Announced Daisy Chain Fields, an all-women music festival donating profits to women’s charities
WHY: To turn joy and music into help for women and girls, inspired by the 1990s Lilith Fair

perspectives.description: They celebrate a concert that puts women’s talents front and center. They believe that every ticket sold helps good causes, so having a great time also does good.
A few people might say a festival that only books women isn’t fair to male musicians, but others answer that the goal is to spotlight female artists who often get less attention.
They see this as a modern version of Lilith Fair, which proved in the 1990s that women could headline huge tours and raise serious money for charities. The tradition continues today.
